newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bank shares surge but market closes lower.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bank shares surge but market closes lower.

text.p: Banking shares on the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday attracted a sudden burst of interest, boosting market activity, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8458.29, down from 8459.29 on Monday.
Dealers attributed the surge in interest to speculation, adding that bearish sentiments still pervaded the market.
Most banks closed higher, led by UBA which rose 10 kobo to 11.40 naira on a rally sparked by investor interest in its recent reorganization.
However, First Bank fell two kobo to 13.26 naira, while Union Bank lost 10 kobo to 10.70 naira and Afribank was down five kobo to 6.40 naira.
Gainers were Wema Bank, up three kobo at 3.48 naira; FSB International Bank, five kobo higher at 4.60 naira; and Guaranty Trust Bank, up two kobo at 5.12 naira.
Sliding blue chips closed lower as investors continued to shun them, traders said.
Conglomerate PZ Industries fell 10 kobo to 28.20 naira, West African Portland Cement Company slipped by a similar margin and petroleum marketer Agip fell five kobo to 17.45 naira.
Nigerian Ropes went ex-dividend at 1.83 naira, shedding 12 kobo.
